name: bollinger_squeeze_breakout_5s
author: adapted from QuantGen_Subagent_3
thesis: Volatility is cyclical; periods of low volatility (squeeze) are followed by explosive expansion. Breakouts from the squeeze predict the direction of the expansion. Exists because prolonged consolidation builds unexecuted order book resting liquidity.
mechanism: Bollinger band extremes indicate price has moved beyond 2 standard deviations from its recent mean. This typically results from a liquidity-driven overshoot rather than fundamental revaluation. Market makers and statistical arbitrageurs recognize the overshoot and trade against it, while the original directional flow exhausts, creating a natural mean-reversion within 30-90 seconds.

conditions: bb_upper < keltner_upper AND bb_lower > keltner_lower AND close > bb_upper
bb_upper < keltner_upper AND bb_lower > keltner_lower AND close < bb_lower

weaknesses: Fakeouts are common right before the True reversal
Needs strong relative volume to confirm, otherwise it flatlines
Difficult to define a tight stop loss due to volatility expansion
adaptation_notes: Converted from 15min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 180x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
